messages.subject: Re: Using Phi coprocessors with RRO
parts: I talked to Intel about how it only uses cores not hyperthreads. I can force the MKL to use everything. But, it might actually slow down the calculations. There is an automatic offload option that Intel uses.  I don't need to use MPSS with RRO, unless I plan on using my Phis.

messages.author: 67f7081cbd450705
messages.subject: Re: Using Phi coprocessors with RRO
parts:
According to Intel, they have options for forcing computations onto the Phis. They also claim that the MKL will send calcs to the Phis, automatically, when the MKL decided the calc is large enough. I guess it tries to determine what is "best" for your system. 

Have you tried exceedingly large matrix calcs? I've been working on large matrices say 100,000x100,000 and raising them to large powers, like 10,000. (I had to reinstall everything on my Phi workstation after I did my benchmarking. If I turned the Phis off 'Automatic_Offload = 0', RRO used 1% of my processor, or less.) When I get it up an running again, I will look at how large you need to go to get the Phis to do their thing.

Another option is to use the AMD ACML. From what I have read, it has an automatic offload option onto GPUs and possibly the Phis. It uses OpenCl to do this. I purchased a couple powerful and cheap AMD GPUs. I'm taking a class this fall in C++ with the hopes it will make me a better programmer when it comes to compiling the ACML. 

Have you read about the newer generation of Phis? The Knights Landing version can actually replace the main processor on your board. They also have huge amounts of DDR4 ECC Ram. One item I saw had 384GB of Ram.
